chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: Why he had never married before Mildred
summary: Never serious about a girl before, he says that absorbed in music he never married; Dance asks how marriage entered.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Yeah. Well listen, well we've got to go back from there for a little while. So, really you and Mildred had been going out together, listening to music and everything, for maybe a year and a half or so, by then.
I suppose about a year or so --
Something like that, yes. A year or so. So then how did the idea of marriage hit you? What -- did you start thinking more about it, or what -- how did the -- you'd never been married, Red?
Pardon?
You had never been married?
No.
And had you ever been serious about any girl or anything, or was music your big love or how was that?
No, I don't think I was ever that serious with -- no I don't think so. I was serious with a couple of girls --
No?
-- but I don't know the way I was moving around, just never seemed to be the right thing.
Yeah.
-- never get married -- I don't know at that time.
Well, I mean the thing is you were so absorbed in music, I guess --
I guess so.
-- and maybe Mildred was the first one that you ever cared about where you shared the same thoughts.
There was a girl in my hometown that
I was very fond of. I Suppose if I wasn't in music that could've developed. Also I knew somebody in vaudeville in show business that I could've very well went that way.
Yeah.
But --
Course, you were pretty young.
Yeah -- I don't --
Early 20's.
-- in -- I was now at that time -- really trying to figure years, it's a little hazy with years --
It's hard, I know it's hard.
The exact years.
Ah --
Although I did know that at the time --
Well let's see --
